title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: REGGIE'S SKATES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Reggie Moreno, a retired city bus mechanic from Fort Wayne, Indiana.
Forty years ago, he met his wife Rosemary at the Roller Dome. She skated circles around him.
Now their fortieth anniversary was coming.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: TOO OLD?
segments.quote: To me, old age is always fifteen years older than I am.
segments.author: Bernard Baruch
lines: Reggie's plan: surprise her at the rink, and skate their song one more time.
His nephew laughed. Tío, you're sixty-six. Your knees sound like bubble wrap.
But Reggie remembered a line from Bernard Baruch, an adviser to presidents:
To me, old age is always fifteen years older than I am.
He bought thrift store skates. Eighteen dollars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FLOOR
segments.quote: If you only knock long enough and loud enough at the gate, you are sure to wake up somebody.
segments.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
lines: Thursday night, Reggie hit the floor six times in ten minutes.
The rink manager, Keisha, said, Sir, the floor is not a bed.
On the wall hung a sign from Henry Wadsworth Longfellow:
If you only knock long enough and loud enough at the gate, you are sure to wake up somebody.
So he came back every Thursday, until Keisha started teaching him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: NACHO CHEESE
segments.quote: Every time a man smiles, but much more so when he laughs, it adds something to this fragment of life.
segments.author: Laurence Sterne
lines: One night, he rolled straight into the snack bar, and wore the nacho cheese.
A birthday party of grown women stared.
Then he thought of the English writer Laurence Sterne:
Every time a man smiles, but much more so when he laughs, it adds something to this fragment of life.
So Reggie laughed the loudest. The women helped him up, and now they cheer him on.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE DAY AT A TIME
segments.quote: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Two weeks left. What if he fell in front of Rosemary?
Keisha showed him words from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
So he stopped counting down, and just skated each night for that night.
And one Thursday, he went all the way around without grabbing the wall.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THEIR SONG
segments.quote: A successful marriage requires falling in love many times, always with the same person.
segments.author: Mignon McLaughlin
lines: Anniversary night, he drove Rosemary to the Roller Dome.
The DJ played their song, and Reggie rolled out to her, steady and proud.
He thought of what the writer Mignon McLaughlin said:
A successful marriage requires falling in love many times, always with the same person.
Rosemary opened her bag. Inside were her old white skates, kept for forty years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LUCKIEST MAN
segments.quote: Today, I consider myself the luckiest man on the face of the earth.
segments.author: Lou Gehrig
lines: Halfway around, they both went down, right in the middle of the floor.
Lying there, laughing, Reggie remembered baseball great Lou Gehrig:
Today, I consider myself the luckiest man on the face of the earth.
The birthday ladies clapped.
Now they skate every Thursday. She still skates circles around him.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Ignore the number. Keep knocking. Laugh. Live today. Fall in love again. Count your luck.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Ignore the number. Keep knocking. Laugh at yourself. Live today. Fall in love again. Count your luck.
Me? I tried skating once. The rink still has a dent shaped like Marco.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
